methodological_rigor.justification: Single-center retrospective cohort of 400 consecutive PDs (2017-2025, with RPD introduced in 2020) using 1:1 PSM on preoperative biliary drainage, neoadjuvant chemotherapy, primary disease, vascular reconstruction, and pancreatic texture (with caliper 0.20), yielding 117 matched pairs. AUC for PSM model was 0.787, an acceptable discrimination. Uses logistic regression for TO predictors with multivariate adjustment. Limitations forthrightly acknowledged: chronological bias (RPD started 2020; OPD spans entire period), higher trainee involvement in OPD, unmeasured confounding, and single-center single-proctor RPD. PSM includes pancreatic texture (intraoperative variable), which authors justify but which may induce collider bias.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: RPD vs OPD for pancreatoduodenectomy is an active clinically and financially consequential surgical question. TO is an established composite quality metric. The striking differences (major complications 17.1% vs 44.4%, POPF 2.6% vs 28.2%, LOS 13 vs 22 days) are clinically meaningful and benchmark-comparable. Findings from an expert high-volume center with LAELAPS-3 training reasonably inform adoption strategy for other centers. As a single-center PSM retrospective comparative cohort, LoE maps to 4 (low-quality cohort).

reporting_quality.justification: Appropriate standard is STROBE for a comparative observational study; not explicitly cited. Ethics approval number provided (2110-002), ERAS protocol detailed, standard definitions used (Clavien-Dindo, ISGPS POPF, ISGLS bile leakage), and benchmark comparison included (Table 4). Key TO components and complication grading are clearly defined. No data or code availability statement; patient-level data not shared. Some methodological details (e.g., handling of missing preoperative variables, variable encoding for logistic regression) are sparse.

novelty_literature.justification: Authors claim novelty in linking robotic surgery with TO achievement. Multiple meta-analyses (Zhang 2021, Zhao 2018, Fu 2022, Waseem 2025) and a related Lee 2025 PSM study on robotic vs laparoscopic TO already exist. The contribution here is incremental: Japanese high-volume center data, TAKUMI-7 training context, and inclusion of intraoperative confounders (pancreatic texture) in PSM. Moderately novel but not paradigm-shifting.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written, well-structured, and appropriately hedged. Tables cover baseline characteristics, outcomes, TO predictors, and a benchmark comparison. Authors are candid about the chronological and trainee-assignment biases. Minor issues: inconsistent use of 'cofounder' for 'confounder', and the CR-POPF 2.6% vs 28.2% difference warrants more scrutiny or a sensitivity analysis in text. Figures of RPD uptake are informative.

key_strengths: Substantial high-volume single-center cohort (n=400; 117 matched pairs) with consistent ERAS protocol since 2014 and standardized LAELAPS-3-based RPD training
PSM incorporated both preoperative and key intraoperative variables (pancreatic texture, vascular reconstruction) with acceptable discrimination (AUC 0.787)
Clinically meaningful and consistent benefit pattern for RPD across operative time, blood loss, LOS, major complications, POPF, and TO achievement
Direct benchmarking against published RPD series (Table 4)
Transparent acknowledgement of chronological, trainee-involvement, and single-proctor biases
key_concerns: Chronological bias: RPD cohort entirely post-2020, while OPD spans 2017-2025, meaning learning effects, technology, and perioperative care improvements co-vary with approach

Surgeon-skill confounding: RPD exclusively performed by board-certified experts (mainly one proctor, KT) whereas OPD included trainee involvement, making group-level comparisons partially a surgeon-experience comparison

CR-POPF rate of 2.6% in RPD arm is strikingly lower than both OPD here (28.2%) and published benchmarks; a sensitivity analysis or discussion of pancreatic-texture/stent-selection interactions would strengthen the paper
Inclusion of pancreatic texture (intraoperative) in PSM could induce collider bias; no sensitivity analysis excluding it is reported
No data availability or code sharing; short-term outcomes only, long-term/oncologic outcomes deferred
No STROBE checklist or formal ROBINS-I-style risk-of-bias discussion
chief_reviewer.rationale: Well-reported PSM comparison at a Japanese high-volume center with clinically meaningful short-term benefits for RPD, constrained by chronological and surgeon-experience confounding; suitable for a Tier 3 surgical/specialty oncology journal with minor revisions including sensitivity analyses and longer-term follow-up plans.
